limits: Covers the verdict /cpp:status and /cpp:update read: a checkout at the tip of origin/main reads current (exit 0), and one commit behind, an unreachable origin, and a checkout the fetch cannot write each read something that is NOT current. `unknown: <reason>` counts as a detection on purpose: for this instrument an honest unknown IS the finding, and the defect being controlled is an unknown rendered as clean. Cases are git SITUATIONS, built fresh by run-case.sh from a one-word committed scenario, because a nested repository cannot be committed. DECLARED GAPS: ahead/diverged and the detached-HEAD/empty-branch paths are pinned by tests/test_cpp_checkout_freshness.py, not registered here; the read-only case is UNAVAILABLE under root, which ignores file modes; the timeout path is not exercised (it needs a remote that hangs, which cannot be built cheaply and deterministically). Nothing here runs against a real host checkout - that confirmation is host-side and owed to the operator (#1282).

anchors.why: The pre-fix logic lived in a markdown fence, not a script, so there was no file to vendor byte-for-byte. The anchor is lines 148-166 of update.md at 164fdd4 reproduced VERBATIM between markers, plus a constructed three-line preamble supplying the gate's calling convention and the `cd`/CURRENT_BRANCH the command set before the block. It prints prose and always exits 0, so it misses every bad case - and on bad-fetch-fails it prints 'Already up to date!' against a remote that is one commit ahead, which is the #1282 defect itself: an unchecked fetch followed by a count against the stale ref. That miss is what makes the post-fix BAD a change in the instrument rather than in the cases.
